ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: There are two horizontal straight lines p and q in the figure, and they are parallel; two blue slanted lines cross above, forming a triangle/exterior-angle structure related to the lower parallel line. ∠1 is marked near the intersection on the lower left with line q, ∠3 is marked near the intersection on the lower right with line q, and ∠2 is marked at the exterior-angle position where the two slanted lines meet above. Then reason: Because p ∥ q, ∠1 = 50° and ∠3 = 60° can be transferred into the two remote interior angles of this triangle through corresponding-angle or alternate-interior-angle relationships of parallel lines. According to the exterior angle theorem, exterior angle ∠2 equals the sum of these two remote interior angles, so m∠2 = 50° + 60° = 110°.

Use the parallel-line relationships to transfer the given measures so the two remote interior angles of that triangle are 50° and 60°. Then apply the exterior angle theorem: an exterior angle equals the sum of its two remote interior angles, so m∠2 = 50 + 60 = 110.
